doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Moving from tenor to alto and into New York studios
summary: Switching to alto made little difference; he moved into studios and Broadway without missing a payday.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Were you happy switching from the tenor to the alto?

It didn’t make much difference. But I would have made a lot more money if I’d have quit then. Yeah, if I’d have left. Because things were more busy in New York you know. And then, but as it turned out it was all right. Because New York wasn’t as busy when I quit five years later, but I made the transition without raising the pay.

Yeah and into Broadway. Yeah and studio work. I went from one thing to the other without missing a payday. But if I’d quit earlier, I would have made a lot more money because there was a lot more things happening in New York at that time, commercially you know.
